knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper proposes a deep-learning-enabled framework for hybrid precoding in mmWave massive MIMO systems to address the high computational complexity and limited spatial exploitation of existing schemes. The method uses a deep neural network to map precoder selections, aiming to minimize bit error ratio and enhance spectrum efficiency. The authors are affiliated with Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications and Tohoku University.

Deep learning is proposed as a superior alternative for handling non-convex problems and exploiting channel sparsity to improve precoding performance.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper proposes a deep-learning-based framework for hybrid precoding in mmWave massive MIMO systems, utilizing a deep neural network as an autoencoder to reduce computational complexity. The system model defines a base station with a uniform linear array and a user, characterized by specific antenna and RF chain constraints. The channel is modeled using the Saleh-Valenzuela model, incorporating line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight components with defined steering vectors.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The mmWave massive MIMO channel exhibits low-rank characteristics due to limited scattering, allowing near-optimal throughput with limited RF chains. The system employs a hybrid precoding structure with high-dimensional analog and low-dimensional digital components, subject to constant modulus and power constraints. A deep neural network (DNN) is utilized to construct a novel precoding framework that exploits the sparsity of the mmWave channel.

It demonstrates that the proposed method achieves lower computational complexity compared to conventional schemes like SIC-based and spatially sparse precoding. The numerical results utilize the Keras framework with specific simulation parameters including a 28 GHz carrier frequency and 45,000 training iterations.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The deep-learning-based hybrid precoding scheme outperforms conventional SVD and GMD methods in bit error ratio (BER) and spectrum efficiency. Performance optimization requires careful selection of batch size and learning rate to balance convergence speed and stability. The proposed method demonstrates superior accuracy and faster convergence compared to analog and sparse precoding approaches.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The proposed deep-learning-based hybrid precoding scheme outperforms analog and sparse precoding methods in spectrum efficiency and Mean Square Error (MSE). The DNN-based approach converges in approximately 11 iterations, whereas the analog precoding scheme requires about 22 iterations. The paper concludes that deep learning enhances hybrid precoding accuracy and reduces computational complexity in mmWave massive MIMO systems.
